info.title: Recoup API - Social
info.description: API documentation for the Recoup platform - an AI agent platform for the music industry

get.description: Retrieve all social media posts from an artist across all platforms. This endpoint aggregates posts from all connected social media profiles for the specified artist, newest first. Engagement counts (`views`, `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`) are the values captured by the most recent scrape of that profile; they are null on platforms that do not report them and on posts stored before engagement capture. Supports pagination for large post collections.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the artist account to fetch posts for

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number to retrieve (default: 1)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of records per page (default: 20, max: 100)

400.description: Bad request - invalid or missing `id` path parameter format

403.description: Forbidden - caller does not have access to this artist

get.description:
Read existing stored comments on posts linked to a creator the caller can access. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential. Caller identity comes from authentication; artist_account_id is the required target creator UUID (the retained wire name), not a caller override. account_id and other unknown or repeated query parameters return 400.

Access uses direct roster, shared-organization and Recoup-administrator checks, plus endpoint-local self-creator and owning-organization-key reads. These read rules do not grant artist mutation permission. Missing and denied targets both return 403. Access is checked on each request; this is not an atomic guarantee against revocation during an executing request. Ownership follows the creator’s linked socials through the post, not the commenter’s social_id. Optional post_id is a stored posts.id UUID, never a URL, and only narrows the authorized linked-post set. An unrelated post or no linked socials returns an empty page; neither permits an unscoped read.

page defaults to 1 and limit to 10; omitted or empty values use these defaults. Both otherwise require positive integers. Larger positive limits are accepted and clamped to 100; pagination.limit reports the effective value. Requests must satisfy page × effective_limit <= 2147483647 or return 400. Comments are ordered by commented_at descending, then id descending. Counts use the same ownership/post filter. Offset pages are deterministic for a fixed dataset, not a frozen snapshot during concurrent changes. A page beyond the results can be empty while retaining a nonzero exact total; no results means total_pages=0. A missing exact count is a 500, not an invented zero.

Each result has only id, post_id, social_id, comment and commented_at. Saved nulls are preserved in the nullable fields; a missing comment author/text is not invented. The stored post join determines inclusion; nullable post_id describes the retained row projection, not permission to read unlinked rows. No joined profile, account or grant metadata is returned. GET success and errors use Cache-Control: private, no-store. Authentication failures are 401; lookup failures are a masked 500 with no unscoped/provider fallback.

This reads saved evidence and does not start scraping, enrichment, billing or comment-writing work. The existing link lookup reads at most 10,000 social links; stored reads do not establish complete ingestion/history, a live report, or the original customer weekly-report journey. The implementation is merged in API #1062; hosted/customer verification remains separate in Mono #327/app #2023.

parameters.description: Required target creator account UUID, using the retained artist wire name. It never overrides the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: post_id
parameters.description: Optional stored posts.id UUID. Narrows the authorized linked-post set; an unrelated stored post returns an empty page. This is not a post URL.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Positive integer page, default 1 for omitted or empty values. page × effective_limit must not exceed 2147483647.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Positive requested page size, default 10 for omitted or empty values. Values above 100 are accepted and clamped to 100; the response reports the effective size.

200.description: Stored comments and exact scoped pagination

get.description: Look up recordings in the Apple Music catalog by ISRC. Accepts up to 25 comma-separated ISRCs per request and returns one row per **requested** ISRC, so a recording that Apple does not carry comes back explicitly as `found: false` rather than being omitted. Complements `GET /api/spotify/search`, which reaches ISRCs only through a fuzzy `isrc:` search query; Apple matches the identifier exactly and additionally returns release-level rights metadata (`upc`, `record_label`, `copyright`) that Spotify does not expose.

parameters.name: isrc
parameters.description: One or more ISRCs, comma-separated. Case-insensitive; each must match the 12-character ISRC format (two-letter country code, three-character registrant code, two-digit year, five-digit designation). Maximum 25 per request.

parameters.name: storefront
parameters.description: Apple Music storefront to search, as a two-letter country code. Availability is territory-specific, so a recording present in one storefront may be absent from another.

200.description: Lookup completed. One entry per requested ISRC, in the order requested.

400.description: Bad request - `isrc` missing, malformed, or over the 25-ISRC limit, or an unknown `storefront`

example.error: isrc must be a valid ISRC: NOTANISRC
Exactly one of x-api-key or Authorization must be provided

500.description: Internal server error, including a failure to reach the Apple Music API

example.error: Failed to reach the Apple Music API

Use the runId returned from endpoints like Instagram Comments, Instagram Profiles, Social Scrape, or Artist Socials Scrape to poll for results.

parameters.name: runId

400.description: Bad request - missing required runId parameter

500.description: Server error - failed to fetch run status from Apify

post.description:
Trigger a scrape of one social profile. Use [Get Artist Socials](/api-reference/artists/socials) first to get the social `id`. The response contains scraper run metadata; poll it with the [Scraper Results API](/api-reference/apify/scraper).

**Credits:** `50,000 + 10,000 × posts` micro-dollar credits per profile: $0.05 base + $0.01 per requested post. Omitting `posts` charges the 50,000 base, even when the selected platform fetches a default depth.

**What `posts` does per platform**

| Platform | `posts` | When `posts` is omitted |
|---|---|---|
| Instagram | ignored | the profile's latest posts (up to 12), always |
| TikTok | `resultsPerPage` | 1 video |
| YouTube | `maxResults`, `maxResultsShorts`, `maxResultStreams` (per content type) | 1 video, 0 Shorts, 0 streams |
| X / Twitter | timeline items; retweets and replies are fetched but not stored | 10 timeline items before filtering |
| LinkedIn | `maxPosts` on the posts actor (runs instead of the profile actor) | profile only, no posts |
| Threads | ignored | profile only |
| Facebook | ignored | profile only |

**What gets stored.** Webhook processing persists supported records from successful runs. Platform filtering, missing fields and budget-limited follow-ups can leave partial results:

- The profile: username, avatar, bio, follower and following counts, region. Served by [Get Artist Socials](/api-reference/artists/socials).
- One follower snapshot per social per day whenever the run reports a follower count (following and post counts too, where the platform reports them). Served by the `history` parameter of Get Artist Socials.
- Every returned post with its engagement (`views`, `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`, where the platform reports them). Served by [Get Artist Posts](/api-reference/posts/get).
- Instagram only: comments batches for already-known and newly discovered posts, then terminal profile batches for the returned commenters. Available profile fields are saved; completion and field coverage are not guaranteed. Served by [Get Artist Fans](/api-reference/fans/get).

**Fan discovery is one hop deep.** The commenter profile run is terminal: it never schedules comments or profile runs of its own. A normal single delivery can produce one profile run, two comments batches and two terminal commenter-profile batches. Five is a derived case, not a universal bound: retries, concurrent deliveries and budget checks affect the outcome. Budget checks are not atomic reservations and may allow overshoot; bookkeeping failures do not guarantee a hard cap. Pass `subtitles=true` on a YouTube social to include each video's transcript in the run results.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the social profile to scrape. Obtain this from the [Get Artist Socials](/api-reference/artists/socials) API.

parameters.name: posts
parameters.description: Recent-post depth. Honored on TikTok, YouTube (per content type), X and LinkedIn; ignored on Instagram (always the profile's latest posts, up to 12), Threads and Facebook. Without it TikTok and YouTube use their single-item defaults; X fetches ten timeline items before filtering, so pass it whenever you need post history. Every returned post is stored with its engagement counts. See the per-platform table above.

parameters.name: subtitles
parameters.description: YouTube only. When `true`, the scrape also downloads each returned video's captions (auto-generated captions preferred, English, plain text). The transcript is returned on the run's dataset items as `subtitles[0].plaintext` and is not persisted; read it from [Scraper Results](/api-reference/apify/scraper) while the run's dataset is available. Ignored on every other platform. Adds no credits beyond the `posts` price.

get.description: List the executable actions available across the authenticated account's connectors. Each action is a single tool that can be invoked via POST /api/connectors/actions — for example, the `googlesheets` connector exposes actions like `GOOGLESHEETS_WRITE_SPREADSHEET`. Actions whose parent connector is not yet connected are returned with `isConnected: false` and cannot be executed until the connector is authorized via POST /api/connectors.

post.description: Execute a connector action with the given parameters. The `actionSlug` must come from a prior call to GET /api/connectors/actions, and `parameters` must match the `parameters` JSON Schema returned for that action. The action's parent connector must be currently connected (`isConnected: true` in the catalog) — otherwise this endpoint returns 409. The `result` field passes through whatever the underlying connector returns; its shape is action-specific. To attach an image to a `file_uploadable` parameter (e.g. `images`), first stage it with [Upload Connector File](/api-reference/connectors/upload-file) and pass the returned descriptor.

403.description: Forbidden — no access to the specified account

409.description: The action's parent connector is not currently connected. Authorize it via POST /api/connectors before retrying.

post.description:
Publish a video with its copy to **one** connected social account, now or at a set time. Send one request per target account; to post the same video to several platforms, call this once per platform.

Without `publish_at` the post starts publishing immediately and is returned as `publishing`. With `publish_at` (a time in the future) it is returned as `scheduled`, starts publishing at that time, and can be cancelled until then with [Cancel Post](/api-reference/publishing/cancel). Either way this returns **202** right away: poll [Get Post](/api-reference/publishing/get) until `status` is `posted`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

The platform must already be connected for the artist in `artist_account_id`, or for the account itself when it is omitted (see [Authorize Connector](/api-reference/connectors/authorize)). Copy uses one shape for every platform. Which fields each platform uses, and their limits:

| Platform | `title` | `description` | `cover_url` | `privacy`, `tags` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `youtube` | **required**, video title, max 100 characters | video description, max 5,000 characters | not used (YouTube picks the frame) | used |
| `instagram` | not used | **required**, Reel caption, max 2,200 characters | Reel cover image | not used |
| `x` | not used | **required**, post text, max 280 weighted characters (URLs count as 23) | not used | not used |
| `linkedin` | video title shown on the post | **required**, post commentary, max 3,000 characters | video thumbnail | not used |

Limits are checked here, so an over-length body fails with 400 instead of at publish time.

Recoup applies no rate limit of its own to this endpoint. Each platform enforces its own caps, and a post over one ends `failed` with the platform's message in `error_message`:

| Platform | Cap |
|---|---|
| `instagram` | 100 API-published posts per account per 24 hours |
| `x` | the X API's per-app and per-user posting limits |
| `youtube` | the daily YouTube Data API upload quota of the connected Google project |
| `linkedin` | LinkedIn's daily per-member and per-organization API limits |

Each post costs **$0.01**, charged to the account the post is made in (`account_id`, or the calling account when omitted), never to the artist. The balance is checked here, so an account without enough credits gets **402** and no post is created. The charge is made only when the post reaches `posted`: a post that ends `failed` or `cancelled` is never charged. A scheduled post is checked against the balance when it is created and charged when it goes live.

202.description: Post accepted: publishing now, or scheduled for `publish_at`.

400.description: Validation failed: a missing or unknown field, a field the platform requires (YouTube `title`; Instagram, X and LinkedIn `description`), a body over the platform's limit, a `publish_at` that is not a date-time with a timezone or is not in the future, or an `account_id` that is an artist (pass it as `artist_account_id`). `missing_fields` names the first offending field.

401.description: Unauthorized. Provide exactly one of `x-api-key` or `Authorization: Bearer`.

402.description: Insufficient credits: the account has less than the $0.01 a post costs. No post is created and nothing is sent to the platform.

403.description: Access denied to the specified `account_id`, or the account has no access to the `artist_account_id`.

409.description: The `platform` is not connected for the artist in `artist_account_id` (or for the account when it is omitted). Authorize it via [Authorize Connector](/api-reference/connectors/authorize) before retrying.

get.description: The platform's own analytics for one post published with [Create Post](/api-reference/publishing/create), read live through the same connection that published it. Currently LinkedIn company-page posts only; other platforms and LinkedIn personal (member) posts return 422. Each call is a fresh read and `as_of` records when it happened. Each successful read costs $0.001 (1,000 credits), charged to the caller after LinkedIn returns the numbers. Credits are checked first; a request that fails (4xx/5xx) is not charged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The post's id, from [Create Post](/api-reference/publishing/create).

402.description: Insufficient credits: the account has less than the $0.001 a read costs. Returned after the 400/401/403/404/409/422 checks and before LinkedIn is called, so nothing is read and nothing is charged.

403.description: Access denied to this post's account.

409.description: The post cannot be read yet. Either it is not published (its status is not `posted` or it has no `post_url`; error `Post is not published yet, so it has no stats`), or the platform is not connected for the post's account (error `linkedin is not connected for this account`). This is checked before 422, so an unpublished post on any platform returns 409.

422.description: Stats are not supported for this post. Only LinkedIn company-page posts are supported today. Errors: `Stats are not available for <platform> posts yet` (any other platform), `Stats are available for LinkedIn company-page posts only` (a LinkedIn personal post), `post_url does not name a LinkedIn post`.

502.description: The platform rejected the stats read, for example because the connection lacks analytics access (error `LinkedIn rejected the stats read for this post`).

SocialInsufficientCreditsResponse.description: Returned (402) when the account lacks credits for the request. Nothing is charged and no Stripe object is created. Credits must be bought explicitly via [`POST /api/credits/sessions`](/api-reference/credits/sessions-create). Examples: a scrape of one profile with posts=20 requires $0.25; one post through Create Post requires $0.01.

billingUrl.description: Static link to the Recoup app, where a human can save a card and buy credits. It is a constant, not a freshly minted Stripe Checkout Session, so a credit-gated endpoint that keeps returning 402 creates nothing. To buy credits programmatically, call [`POST /api/credits/sessions`](/api-reference/credits/sessions-create).

slug.description: Unique identifier for the action — pass this as `actionSlug` when calling POST /api/connectors/actions. Action slugs are always UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. `GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE`, `GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS`, `GOOGLESHEETS_WRITE_SPREADSHEET`).

description.description: What the action does. Use this to pick the right action from the catalog.

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the parameters this action expects. Pass values matching this schema in the `parameters` field of the execute request.

connectorSlug.description: Slug of the parent connector this action belongs to (e.g. 'googlesheets', 'tiktok', 'youtube', 'twitter', 'linkedin'). Matches the `slug` returned by GET /api/connectors.

isConnected.description: Whether the parent connector is currently authorized for this account. Actions can only be executed when this is true.

actions.description: Available actions across all connectors the authenticated account has access to. Both connected and unconnected actions are returned — check `isConnected` per action before attempting execution.

actionSlug.description: Action slug from GET /api/connectors/actions. Always UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. `GOOGLESHEETS_WRITE_SPREADSHEET`). Required.

parameters.description: Action-specific parameters matching the `parameters` JSON Schema returned by GET /api/connectors/actions for this `actionSlug`. The connector validates these against the cached schema before executing — invalid shapes return 400. Required.

account_id.description: Optional account ID to execute the action on a different account (e.g., an artist). The authenticated account must have access. Omit to execute on your own account.

result.description: Pass-through of the underlying connector's response payload. Shape is action-specific — consult the action's parameters schema and the third-party service's own documentation for what to expect. The server-side wrapper does not transform this field.

executedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the action was executed server-side.

url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the image to stage. Fetched server-side and uploaded to Connector storage. Required.

toolSlug.description: The action slug the image will be attached to, UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. `LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST`). Scopes the upload to that tool/toolkit. Required.

mimetype.description: Detected MIME type of the stored file.

s3key.description: Connector storage key. Pass this together with `name` and `mimetype` in the action's file_uploadable array.

PostPlatform.description: Target platform. The account must have this platform connected.

PostStatus.description: Lifecycle phase. `scheduled` until `publish_at`, `publishing` while the platform upload runs, then `posted` or `failed`. `cancelled` only from `scheduled`.

CreatePostRequest.description: One post to one connected account. Copy uses the same fields for every platform; see the operation description for which fields each platform uses and their limits.

account_id.description: Optional. The account the post is made in and charged to. Defaults to the calling account; org admins can pass another account in their organization. Must not be an artist: pass the artist as `artist_account_id`.

artist_account_id.description: Optional. The artist, within the account, whose connected social account posts. The account must have access to the artist. Defaults to the account's own connection. The artist is never charged.

sub_account_id.description: Optional, LinkedIn only. Organization URN to post as a Page (e.g. `urn:li:organization:101127186`) instead of as the connected member. The connected member must be an admin of that Page.

video_url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the video file (MP4). It is fetched at publish time, so it must still resolve then.

cover_url.description: Optional. Publicly reachable image URL used as the cover or thumbnail where the platform supports one (see the table in the description).

title.description: Title. Required for `youtube`; see the table in the description.

description.description: Body text: caption, post text or description, depending on the platform. Required for `instagram`, `x` and `linkedin`.

privacy.description: Optional, YouTube only. Visibility after upload.

publish_at.description: Optional. ISO 8601 time to publish, with a timezone (`Z` or an offset), in the future. Omit to publish now.

CreatePostResponse.description: The post's id and current status.

id.description: The post's id. Poll [Get Post](/api-reference/publishing/get) with this.

account_id.description: The account the post was made in and charged to.

artist_account_id.description: The artist whose connected social account posted, or `null` when the account's own connection posted.

sub_account_id.description: LinkedIn organization URN when posting as a Page, else null.

video_url.description: The video that is or was published.

cover_url.description: The cover or thumbnail image, if any.

publish_at.description: Requested publish time. Null when published on creation.

post_url.description: Live URL on the platform. Null until `posted`.

error_message.description: Why publishing failed, as returned by the platform (e.g. a daily upload quota). Null unless `status` is `failed`.

text_verified.description: Whether the live text, re-read from the platform after posting, equals the submitted `title`/`description`. Null until checked.

platform.description: The platform the post was published to.

impressions.description: Times the post was shown. `null` when the platform does not report it.

unique_impressions.description: Distinct members the post was shown to. `null` when the platform does not report it.

clicks.description: Clicks on the post's content, company name or logo. `null` when the platform does not report it.

likes.description: Likes (reactions). `null` when the platform does not report it.

comments.description: Comments. `null` when the platform does not report it.

shares.description: Reposts. `null` when the platform does not report it.

engagement.description: LinkedIn's engagement rate for the post, from 0 to 1. `null` when the platform does not report it.

video_views.description: Times the post's video was viewed; LinkedIn counts a view at 3 or more seconds. `null` for non-video posts or when LinkedIn returns none.

viewers.description: Distinct members who viewed the post's video. `null` for non-video posts or when LinkedIn returns none.

watch_time_ms.description: Total time the post's video was watched, in milliseconds. `null` for non-video posts or when LinkedIn returns none.

posts.description: Posts, newest first. Empty when the account has none.

missing_fields.description: JSON path segments to the first field that failed validation, e.g. `["description"]`
Validation path, possibly empty for unknown query keys.

error.description: Human-readable error message or documented error code.
